sentences.text: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondent, on account of death of Jainaa Bi, who is mother of petitioners No.1 to 3, in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 19-02-2024 at about 10.40 a.m., deceased Jainaa Bi was pedestrian on the foot path of the Gauribidanur road and she was walking slowly and cautiously, by observing all traffic rules and regulations and vehicular movement, on the extreme side of the road.

When she was infront of Library, Gudibande Town, Gudibande Taluk, Chickballapura, the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F-1255,
drove the same in rash and negligent manner, without observing any traffic rules and regulations, endangering to human life and dashed against the deceased and caused the accident.

Due to said impact, the deceased has sustained severe injuries all over the body and she was shifted to Gudibande Government Hospital, wherein she took first aid treatment and then she was shifted to Chikkaballapura Government Hospital for further treatment, wherein, even after better and expert treatment, the deceased was succumbed to fatal injuries, on the same day at 2.30 p.m. Earlier to the accident

,
the deceased was working as coolie and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
She was contributing her entire earnings to her family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
The Gudibande Police have registered the case against the driver of the said KSRTC Bus for the offence punishable under Section 279 and 304(A) of I.P.C.
The respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondent, the respondent has appeared through his counsel and filed the written statement.

sentences.text: The respondent in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has contended that, there was no nexus between the death of Jainaa Bi and the KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-40-F-1255.

On 19-02-2024, the bus in question was on its schedule trip from Bengaluru to Gudibande and the bus was being driven by its driver slowly and cautiously, on the left side of the road, by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.
While it was so proceeding and when it reached Gudibande bus-stand, the driver stopped the bus so as to enable the passengers to alight from the bus.

At that time, the driver observing a old lady lying on the middle of the road with some injuries and thinking that, she might have fell down on the road, due to faint or giddiness, on the humanitarian ground he shifted the injured to the Government Hospital, Gudibande.

But,
unfortunately the petitioners forgetting the timely help rendered by the crew of the bus, with the sole intention to make an unlawful gain from the respondent, by projecting the death of the deceased as accidental death, involving the bus in question, falsely implicated the bus in question and foisted a false case against the driver of said bus and in active collusion and connivance with the Police has got created false documents.
Under these circumstances the respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

Chikkaballapura, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.
No. KA-40-F-1255 ?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?

sentences.text: While it was so proceeding and when it reached Gudibande bus-stand, the driver stopped the bus so as to enable the passengers to alight from the bus.

At that time, the driver observing a old lady lying on the middle of the road with some injuries and thinking that, she might have fell down on the road, due to faint or giddiness,
on the humanitarian ground he shifted the injured to the Government Hospital, Gudibande.

But, the petitioners in order to get unlawful gain from the respondent, by projecting the death of the deceased as accidental death, falsely implicated the said bus in the alleged accident and foisted a false case against the driver of said bus and in collusion with the Police have foisted a false case against the driver of the said bus.
But, the respondent has failed to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statement of R.W.1, who is the accused/driver of the offending bus at the time of accident, there is absolutely no other oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent to establish the above contentions.
The respondent could have established the said contentions by examining independent eye-witness to the alleged accident.
But, the respondent has not made any efforts or not taken any steps to examine the eye-witness to the alleged accident.

The respondent has failed to prove through cogent and corroborative evidence that, the offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F-1255 was not at all involved in the alleged accident and the petitioners in collusion with the Police have falsely implicated the said bus in the alleged accident.
In such circumstances, it can safely be held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record clearly establishes that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-40-F-1255 and dashing the same to deceased Jainaa Bi, who was walking on the road, 4 feet away from center median of the road, infront of Library, Gudibande Town, Gudibande Taluk, Chickballapura District and due to said impact, the deceased fell down on the road and the rare right side wheel of the said bus ran over her right hand and caused grievous injuries to her right hand and forehead and succumbed to said injuries while undergoing treatment at Government Hospital, Chikkaballapura, on the same day at 2.30 p.m.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the documents got marked by the petitioners themselves,
particularly the Ex.P.3 spot mahazer and Ex.P.4 sketch clearly reveals that, at the time of accident the deceased was walking on the main road, at a distance of 4 feet from the center median of the road, where they were no zebra crossing marks for the pedestrian to walk or to cross the road.

If the deceased had used the foothpath to walk or had taken required care while using the public road,
having proper lookout at the movement of vehicles on the said road, the accident could not have occurred.
This clearly goes to show that, the deceased has contributed in the cause of accident.
As such the deceased is liable to be held responsible for contributory negligence in the cause of accident.
On the other hand, if the driver of offending KSRTC Bus had driven his vehicle in moderate speed, with care and caution, he could have avoided the said accident and saved the life of the deceased.
The driver of a vehicle using public road is having higher duty to exercise reasonable care and observe traffic rules & regulations, including yielding to pedestrians.

In such circumstances, taking into consideration the place of accident and the age of the deceased as on the date of accident being 75 years, this Court is of the opinion that, the negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle is at higher side.
Accordingly, apportioning the negligence on the part of the deceased at 20% and on the part of the driver of offending vehicle at 80% would be justified.

Further it is pertinent to note, as per Ex.P.8 Motor Vehicle Accident Report, the said accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the offending bus and there was no other vehicle involved in the accident, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
14. Further, the Ex.P.7 Post-motem report, clearly speaks that, the deceased Jainaa Bi has died due to head injury sustained in the road traffic accident.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet, which is marked as Ex.P.11 has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-40-F-1255 and deceased Jainaa Bi has succumbed to injuries sustained in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owner or driver of the offending KSRTC Bus.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, with regard to date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-40-F-1255 in the accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle, injuries caused to deceased Jainaa Bi and the cause of her death.
15.

Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held

sentences.text: Issue No.2:

While answering above issue, for the reasons stated therein, this Court has already held that, the petitioners have successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that,
the alleged accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-40-F-1255 and the deceased Jainaa Bi has succumbed to injuries sustained in the said accident.
Now the petitioners are required to establish that, they are the legal representatives of the deceased.
In this regard, they have produced their respective Aadhar cards and Aadhar card of the deceased, which are marked as Ex.P.12 to 15.
The said documents clearly goes to show that, the petitioners No.1 to 3 are the children of deceased Jainaa Bi.
On the other hand, the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased Jainaa Bi is not specifically denied by the respondent and there is no rebuttal evidence with respect to same.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the above documents produced by the petitioners and hold that, the petitioners are the legal representatives of deceased Jainaa Bi.
19.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356, has clearly held that, "The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166(1).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependant on the deceased, would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.
This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra) had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.
The latter part relates to the entitlement of compensation by a person who claims for the same.
It is thus settled by now that, the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."
20.

According to the ratio laid down in above decision, the legal representatives though not fully dependent on the deceased are entitled to claim compensation under all the heads i.e., under both conventional and non-conventional heads.

In order to determine the compensation, the age,
avocation, income, dependency, future prospects of the deceased and other conventional heads are to be ascertained.
21. The compensation towards loss of dependency: The petitioners No.1 to 3 are the children of deceased Jainaa Bi.
The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly established that, they are legal representatives of the deceased Jainaa Bi and they were depending on her income.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
In order to calculate the loss of dependency, the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.

In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

a) The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the cases of, G. T. Basavaraj V/s Niranjan and another, in MFA No.7781/2016, judgment dated 11-08-2022, Ramanna and another V/s Y. B. "when the income of the deceased is not proved, then the notional income as per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is to be adopted as the income of the deceased."
b) Admittedly the accident took place in the year 2024.

opennyai_summary.facts:
She was contributing her entire earnings to her family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
The Gudibande Police have registered the case against the driver of the said KSRTC Bus for the offence punishable under Section 279 and 304(A) of I.P.C.
Hence, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Jainaa Bi W/o Late Abdul Sab, has succumbed to the injuries sustained in vehicular accident, alleged to have been occurred on 19-02-2024, at about 10.40 a.m., infront of Library, Gudibande Town,
Chikkaballapura, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.
No. KA-40-F-1255 ?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?

Issue No.1: Partly Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioners that, on 19-02-2024 at about 10.40 a.m., infront of Library, Gudibande Town, Gudibande Taluk, Chickballapura, the deceased Jainaa Bi was a pedestrian on the foot path of the Gauribidanur road and she was walking slowly and cautiously, by observing all traffic rules and regulations and vehicular movement, on the extreme side of the road.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
If the deceased had used the foothpath to walk or had taken required care while using the public road,
having proper lookout at the movement of vehicles on the said road, the accident could not have occurred.
This clearly goes to show that, the deceased has contributed in the cause of accident.
As such the deceased is liable to be held responsible for contributory negligence in the cause of accident.
On the other hand, if the driver of offending KSRTC Bus had driven his vehicle in moderate speed, with care and caution, he could have avoided the said accident and saved the life of the deceased.
The driver of a vehicle using public road is having higher duty to exercise reasonable care and observe traffic rules & regulations, including yielding to pedestrians.
In such circumstances, taking into consideration the place of accident and the age of the deceased as on the date of accident being 75 years, this Court is of the opinion that, the negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle is at higher side.
Accordingly, apportioning the negligence on the part of the deceased at 20% and on the part of the driver of offending vehicle at 80% would be justified.
Shakeera Bi vs K.S.R.T.C on 5 June, 2025
When the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the offending bus and there was no other vehicle involved in the accident, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
14. Further, the Ex.P.7 Post-motem report, clearly speaks that, the deceased Jainaa Bi has died due to head injury sustained in the road traffic accident.
The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet, which is marked as Ex.P.11 has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-40-F-1255 and deceased Jainaa Bi has succumbed to injuries sustained in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owner or driver of the offending KSRTC Bus.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, with regard to date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-40-F-1255 in the accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle, injuries caused to deceased Jainaa Bi and the cause of her death.
15.
Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held
that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof as in a criminal case are not required
In order to determine the compensation, the age,
avocation, income, dependency, future prospects of the deceased and other conventional heads are to be ascertained.
The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly established that, they are legal representatives of the deceased Jainaa Bi and they were depending on her income.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
In order to calculate the loss of dependency, the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
As per the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 S.C., the appropriate multiplier in the present case is taken as 5.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, the notional income of the deceased as per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is to be treated as Rs.15,500/- per month.
After deducting 1/3rd out of total income,
towards the personal expenses of deceased, the annual income of the deceased is held as Rs.1,24,000/-.
Accordingly, the compensation under the head of loss of dependency is held as Rs.6,20,000/-.
Hence, the petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation under the head of parental consortium.
a ) Loss of estate - Rs. 15,000/-
 b) Loss of consortium - Rs. 40,000/-
 c) Funeral expenses - Rs. 15,000/-
The compensation under above heads has to be enhanced 10% for every 3 years.
Seven years have been lapsed from the date of the judgment.
Therefore, the compensation under the above conventional heads is enhanced by 20%, the loss of estate comes to Rs.18,000/-, the loss of parental consortium comes to Rs.48,000/- each to petitioners No.1 to 3 and funeral expenses comes to Rs.18,000/-.
22.
Accordingly, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
 Sl. Head of  Amount/Rs  No. Compensation  1. Loss of dependency Rs. 6,20,000-00  2. Loss of filial consortium Rs. 1,44,000-00  3. Loss of estate Rs. 18,000-00
4 . Funeral expenses Rs. 18,000-00
Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.6,40,000/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
In such circumstances, the respondent being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
holding that, the petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation of Rs.6,40,000/- from the respondent, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.6,40,000/- (Rupees six lakh forty thousand only), with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent is liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioners and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.
The above compensation amount is apportioned as follows:
Petitioner No.1- Daughter - 35% Petitioner No.2- Daughter- 35% Petitioner No.3 - Son - 30%
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest awarded in favour of petitioners No.1 to 3 shall be released in their favour through e- payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
